The Árni Magnússon Institute for Icelandic Studies offers a scholarship for international students and scholars of Icelandic — language, literature and history — to support a research stay in Reykjavík. The institute publishes the annual call and its closing date on the scholarship page.

Programme Highlights

  • Prestigious niche scholarship for Icelandic language and manuscript studies
  • Research-stay support at Iceland's national institute for Icelandic studies
  • Access to the Arnamagnænan manuscript collections
  • Annual call with a fixed closing date on the institute's site

Who Should Apply

International students and researchers of Icelandic language, literature or history at master's level or beyond, with a defined research plan.

Funding and Costs

Monthly grant towards a research stay in Reykjavík, per the conditions on the institute's page. Confirm the exact funding package on the official page before applying.

Deadline and How to Apply

Check the institute's scholarship page for the current call, closing date and application requirements. Key deadline information: Annual call — the closing date is published on the institute's scholarship page.

Official Link

  • Official application page (verified link)

About Árni Magnússon Institute for Icelandic Studies

The Árni Magnússon Institute for Icelandic Studies is Iceland's national centre for research and teaching in Icelandic language, literature and manuscript heritage, offering scholarships to international scholars.

Official website: https://www.arnastofnun.is

Contact

Questions about this position, eligibility or the application process should be raised through the contact channel given on the official announcement page (see the Official Link section above). Always quote the position reference in your message so the admissions or HR team can route your enquiry quickly.

Important Notes

  • Application deadline: Annual call - see official page - late or incomplete applications are normally not considered.
  • Listing details were recorded from the official source at the time of publication; always confirm the latest requirements on the official page before applying.
  • Prepare the documents listed in the eligibility and application sections before starting the online form - transcripts, CV and references take the longest to collect.
